And flesh that separated from a living animal — in Laws of Kings the Rambam ruled that also for a child of Noah flesh that separated from a living animal is forbidden; and Kesef Mishneh wondered: behold its prohibition is from the verse flesh in the field treifah; until they said one who eats eivar min hachai and flesh from a living animal receives two sets of lashes; and if so, what is the nature of a child of Noah for this prohibition of treifah — is a child of Noah commanded regarding treifah, see there; and even though his words are correct, nevertheless the difficulty is not on the Rambam but on the Gemara, for R' Yehudah derives it for him from this verse flesh in the field, etc.; and this is that a child of Noah is forbidden in flesh that separated from a living animal, as is explicit in the chapter of the hide and the sauce explicitly; and if so, the difficulty is on R' Yehudah from this baraita of hide and sauce. Therefore one must reconcile the words of the Gemara plainly — and it is certainly the plain meaning of the verse you shall not eat soul with flesh — it teaches regarding flesh from a living animal, for who mentions a limb; therefore R' Yehudah holds this prohibition of a child of Noah that is written in it flesh with its soul, its blood you shall not eat — we say it comes on what is reasonable regarding eivar min hachai according to the plain meaning of the verse, for flesh in the field is not written in it treifah; and what relevance does a child of Noah have to treifah; and if you say if so, from where do we know eivar min hachai — one can say: since flesh from a living animal was forbidden, eivar min hachai in which there is flesh, sinews, and bones is plainly forbidden, and we learn two things; and if flesh from a living animal requires an olive-bulk of flesh, and eivar min hachai is a minute amount of flesh with sinews and bones — this applies to Israel who requires an olive-bulk; but a child of Noah who is in a minute amount, as the Rambam wrote that measures were stated only for Israel — if so, a minute amount of flesh is also included in flesh from a living animal; therefore for a child of Noah flesh from a living animal and limb from a living animal come from one verse, as written; but for Israel one cannot derive limb from flesh, for in this an olive-bulk is required and in this not — therefore the Torah specified a separate prohibition flesh in the field, etc.; and one comes for eivar min hachai and one for flesh — unlike a child of Noah, one need not derive limb from flesh; and requires further study. In this one can say that R' Yehudah derives flesh from a living animal from flesh in the field treifah, and Rashi explained he derives from you shall not eat soul with flesh, etc.; they go according to their views: for Resh Lakish the above difficulty is difficult — from where do we forbid both for a child of Noah, limb and flesh; and if as above R' Yehudah does not hold that measures were not stated for a child of Noah — for Resh Lakish holds half a measure is permitted from the Torah; and it is difficult: who is there anything forbidden for an idolater in half a measure and permitted for Israel — for Resh Lakish entirely; and necessarily measures were also stated for a child of Noah; and if so, the above difficulty is in its place — from where do we know limb and flesh for a child of Noah; and necessarily it must be said one verse flesh with its soul, etc. includes both limb and flesh; and so for Israel — unlike R' Yehudah who does not hold measures were stated for a child of Noah, and the difficulty who is there anything does not apply — for for Israel in any case half a measure is forbidden; and if so, one can well say as above that for a child of Noah one verse suffices for flesh and for limb, and for Israel two verses, as above. (And behold Mishneh Lamelech in Laws of Chametz and Laws of Oaths debated the words of Raavan whose view is that plain eating is any amount, only tradition extracted that liability is only in an olive-bulk; and he wondered on him and debated him; and also Mishneh Lamelech; and from the above it is proven that if plain eating is in an olive-bulk, how can there be for a child of Noah in any amount — behold eating is written in the verse, and plain eating is in an olive-bulk; and necessarily plain eating is in a minute amount, only Mishneh Lamelech extracted it; and regarding a child of Noah where there is no tradition in a minute amount (and see Mishneh Lamelech that he himself admits for Resh Lakish it does not exist, and plain eating is in an olive-bulk; and if so, it is plain that he holds that also for a child of Noah an olive-bulk is required, for eating is stated in it; and requires further study). And afterward I found in the chapter of the hide and the sauce that Rashba brought this difficulty in the name of Ramban: how is the idolater liable for flesh from a living animal that is derived for R' Yehudah from flesh in the field treifah, etc.; and he answered that the verse stated regarding a child of Noah includes both limb and flesh; but the verse stated regarding Israel includes only limb and not flesh, see there. And behold one can challenge that which they challenge at the beginning of chapter 2 of Pesachim on R' Eliezer who said you shall not eat — even prohibition of benefit is implied; and behold eivar min hachai that is written you shall not eat, etc. — and from where that a person should not give eivar min hachai to an idolater, as it is said lifnei iver do not place a stumbling block; the reason is lifnei iver is forbidden, but otherwise it is permitted; and it is forbidden in benefit, etc.; and it is difficult: perhaps it deals with flesh from a living animal; or we derive from flesh in the field treifah you shall not eat — this is prohibition of benefit is not implied, for treifah the Merciful permitted to dogs you shall cast it; but for a child of Noah it is forbidden as above, and there is lifnei iver, etc.; and if he cited because of eivar min hachai and did not cite flesh from a living animal — this is borrowed language and inclusive, as written in tractate Sanhedrin: a child of Noah is commanded regarding eivar min hachai and counted it among seven commandments, and does not specify flesh from a living animal, for all is included in eivar min hachai (and perhaps one can reject: since all concern is in flesh from a living animal, for even its benefit is forbidden, it was not appropriate to be concise; and it is strained). And behold one can reconcile this difficulty from the Gemara of Pesachim (and see similarly that he labored to give a reason why measures were not stated for a child of Noah — and it is not needed, the matter is simple, for this half measure was included for R' Yochanan from the verse whoever eats chelev, and this was not stated for a child of Noah; and so the language of the Rambam, for measures were given only to Israel, teaches thus; and the matter is as written, for plain eating means a minute amount); and according to what I wrote, therefore a child of Noah is liable for flesh because the plain meaning of the verse is reasonable on flesh; and that which we do not say so for Israel — for a verse for flesh from a living animal was not needed, it is already derived from the inclusive rule of flesh in the field, etc.; if so, it is difficult: these that there is no difference between the prohibition flesh in the field treifah, etc., and the prohibition you shall not eat soul with flesh; but if we say you shall not eat — prohibition of benefit is implied, but in treifah only prohibition of eating, as written you shall cast to dogs, etc.; if so, one can say forever you shall not eat soul applies to flesh from a living animal like a child of Noah; and if it is difficult: behold we already derived from flesh in the field treifah — this is not difficult, the intent of the Torah was to forbid it in benefit, and therefore it wrote you shall not eat the soul with the flesh, and prohibition of benefit is implied; but from this verse flesh in the field, etc., it is only prohibition of eating like other treifot; and the difficulty is in its place: perhaps you shall not eat applies only to flesh from a living animal; and necessarily according to his view this inclusive rule does not exist, that the plain meaning of the verse is more reasonable to explain on flesh than what we explained on flesh; and on the contrary on limb and not on flesh; and not like the baraita of hide and sauce. And if so, it comes out well that according to his view the plain meaning of the verse is more reasonable to explain on limb than what we explained on flesh; and accordingly even for a child of Noah one can say so (this is all according to what is written, and not like Ramban); and in truth one must say according to his view that children of Noah are permitted in flesh that separated, for there is no verse here; and it comes out well according to his view that you shall not eat for R' Eliezer — eivar min hachai is forbidden in benefit; if so, it is proven from what is written that this verse you shall not eat soul with flesh is the plain meaning of the verse on eivar min hachai; and this verse flesh in the field is on flesh from a living animal — there is no prohibition of flesh from a living animal for a child of Noah; and R' Eliezer does not hold this baraita in the chapter of hide and sauce; and the Gemara challenges well: why need flesh from a living animal, for it is not relevant for lifnei iver, for it is not stated for a child of Noah; and the Gemara answers: eivar min hachai is permitted in benefit; and if so, we return to the above that flesh from a living animal is more reasonable only for Israel we derive from and flesh in the field, etc.; and the law is true law: flesh from a living animal is forbidden for a child of Noah; and requires further study. And by way of sharpening for students I would say on this difficulty that we challenged above, Laws of slaughter siman 27 — why does the Gemara challenge in Pesachim, and behold eivar min hachai, etc. — perhaps R' Natan who said from where that one should not give, etc., holds like the Sages that it does not apply in impurity; and this is for Israel; but for a child of Noah it is forbidden, as Rav's statement there; and if so, R' Natan deals with eivar min hachai of impure animal that Israel was not commanded at all, all the more so there is no prohibition of benefit; but for a child of Noah it is forbidden to give because of lifnei iver, for a child of Noah is commanded regarding it; and see what I wrote in its reconciliation; and one can say that he holds this that an idolater is forbidden in eivar min hachai of impure animal is not in the chapter of the hide — this one who holds still convulsing is permitted for a child of Noah even though slaughter is not relevant, because of the reason who is there anything; see there Gemara and Tosafot Chullin daf 28 what they wrote on this. If so, the same applies in impurity; and that which Tosafot wrote nevertheless for Israel it is forbidden because of impurity — the Gemara strains: what relevance does this have to that; in the end regarding this eivar min hachai prohibition it is relevant who is there anything. But all this is if the Torah's decree whoever its flesh is permitted etc. — eivar min hachai does not apply in Israel in impurity; if so, one can well say the same for a child of Noah who is there anything; but if the reason is because prohibition does not apply to prohibition — if so, for a child of Noah where this is not relevant, for he has no impurity prohibition, it is plain that it applies; and as we say this is the reason he gave; and if so, there is no answer that according to his view who holds there is prohibition of benefit in eivar min hachai — if so, a reason is needed why eivar min hachai does not apply to impurity, for there is no because prohibition does not apply to prohibition, for there is an additional prohibition from miggo that it applies to prohibition of benefit, etc., that impurity is permitted in benefit, and additional prohibition — according to all prohibition applies to prohibition; and it must be said the Torah's decree lest eivar min hachai apply in impurity whose flesh is forbidden; and if so, also for a child of Noah it is not forbidden who is there anything, etc.; and the Gemara challenges well from that which one should not give, etc. — for according to his view, eivar min hachai of impurity is not relevant for a child of Noah like for Israel; but according to the conclusion that it is permitted in benefit — if so, there is no additional prohibition; and if so, prohibition does not apply to prohibition — one can well say for a child of Noah even in impurity eivar min hachai applies, and who is there anything does not apply; and for Israel the reason is because prohibition does not apply to prohibition; and there is no answer; and requires further study.
From a living animal. And Tur wrote that it does not apply in impure animals; and Bach wondered: what practical difference for practical law — in the end it is forbidden because of impurity; and see what the later authorities wrote. And if one says the practical difference is whether one receives lashes or prohibition in general — regarding disqualification of testimony, as explained in Choshen Mishpat siman 34, see there; requires further study: if one ate a limb in which in combination of flesh, bone, and sinew there is only an olive-bulk, he does not receive lashes because of impurity, but because of eivar min hachai he receives lashes and is disqualified for testimony — a great practical difference. Also if he swore he will not eat this limb and there is in it a minute amount of flesh, etc. — it applies to impurity, for an oath applies to half a measure; and see below siman 238; and that which Shach wrote the practical difference regarding a sick person whether they need to release the oath — but if eivar min hachai applies, behold he swore to uphold a d'oraisa matter and it does not apply at all, and release is not needed, for eivar min hachai applies in impurity. However, in any case one can say: an apostate Israelite — it is common regarding limbs of impure animal; but it is not common regarding limbs from a living animal; and it is known that lifnei iver prohibition is only where apart from this it is not common regarding the prohibition; and as we say it stands on two sides of the river; and if so, if it is forbidden only because of impurity, it is permitted to give to an apostate; and regarding lifnei iver there is nothing in it, for impure limbs are common regarding it, and there is no lifnei iver in it; but if they are also forbidden because of eivar min hachai — this is not common regarding the apostate, and it is forbidden to give him because of lifnei iver, etc.; and a great practical difference; and easy negotiation.
Forbidden — if the animal is treifah, if eivar min hachai applies to treifah (and practical difference as I wrote above regarding apostate and the like) — we say in Chullin daf 33: one who ate eivar min hachai and from treifah — R' Yehudah said he is liable for two; and Resh Lakish said he is liable only for one; and Rava established it like his view against Abbaye, who deals with one who plucked a limb and rendered it treifah in it; and the animal — the prohibition does not stand for limbs; and if so, treifah prohibition and limb prohibition come together; and Resh Lakish holds the prohibition stands for limbs, and treifah prohibition did not come and apply to eivar min hachai; and afterward the Gemara concluded in the name of R' Yochanan: he plucked chelev from treifah and it lived and he ate it — he receives three lashes; and the Gemara was divided on the reason of the matter — whether because the prohibition stands for limbs and all three applied as one; and it deals with that it became treifah immediately at birth; or the prohibition does not stand for limbs, and eivar min hachai prohibition applied to treifah and chelev; and see there another establishment. And behold the Rambam in Forbidden Foods chapter 5 halachah 8 wrote: one who plucked a limb from a living animal and rendered it treifah in removing it and ate it — he is liable for two because of eivar min hachai and because of treifah, for two prohibitions came as one; from this it is implied that the Rambam holds the prohibition does not stand for limbs; and eivar min hachai is not considered an inclusive prohibition, since it applies to a child of Noah; for otherwise how did they apply as one — behold eivar min hachai applied immediately at birth; and also if eivar min hachai were an inclusive prohibition, what of it that it was treifah from before — behold it would be an inclusive prohibition; and also at first glance it is astonishing, for the Rambam himself holds inclusive prohibition; and it is difficult like Tosafot's difficulty on R' Yochanan; and also afterward the Rambam wrote: one who plucks chelev and ate it receives two lashes because of chelev and because of eivar min hachai (and this is difficult, since the prohibition does not stand for limbs, chelev prohibition preceded from exiting to the air of the world — how can eivar min hachai prohibitions apply, behold I have no inclusive prohibition either); he plucked chelev from treifah and ate it — he receives three lashes; necessarily; and this is more difficult, since the prohibition does not stand for limbs, how can eivar min hachai prohibition apply to chelev and treifah, for behold I have no inclusive prohibition either, and treifah in it was not mentioned. And already Lechem Mishneh and authors stood on it; and they reconciled strainedly, as Peri Chadash wrote; and Peri Chadash also explained strainedly, and understanding is difficult. And what appears to me: it is certainly difficult how Rava can say to R' Yehudah if not eivar min hachai and treifah prohibitions come as one — he is not liable for limb and for treifah; and afterward R' Yochanan stated simply that he is liable for limb and treifah; therefore it appears that this is the Rambam's view: for there to be inclusive prohibition because it applies to a child of Noah — we do not say as I wrote above that a prohibition stated regarding children of Noah is not a prohibition for which Israel is liable; and he holds that which we say the animal while alive stands for limbs — and Rashi explained: to cut it into pieces; and one must explain how it stands to cut it — for if one cuts it, the pieces are forbidden because of eivar min hachai; and from the Torah you shall destroy the animal — and it must be said that thus are the matters: were it not that the Torah forbade because of eivar min hachai, the animal would stand to be cut as he wishes, only the Torah forbade because of eivar min hachai and it is impossible to cut it; therefore on every piece and piece eivar min hachai applies lest he cut it and cut from it; and the Rambam holds this applies when other pieces and limbs in the body stand to be cut, were it not for the Merciful One's prohibition of eivar min hachai; but a limb that renders treifah in it in the body — such as thigh and the like — if so, how can it be thought to cut — who is crazy and foolish who would cut a limb and render treifah thereby the whole animal. And this is certainly not for cutting and limbs remain; and this is what Rava innovated: certainly in general the prohibition stands for limbs and treifah prohibition did not come and apply; but in one who cuts a limb that renders treifah in it — this is certainly the prohibition does not stand for limbs, and treifah prohibition applied, for it is prohibition in a single body; and this is what R' Yehudah holds in such a case the prohibition does not stand for limbs; and if so, now that we were informed of a limb that renders treifah in it, such as thigh and the like — the prohibition does not stand for limbs; and if so, an animal that became treifah — all such limbs, treifah prohibition applied to them, for they did not stand for limbs; and at the time of treifah it applied to them, for then he can pluck them; for otherwise the animal is treifah; and if so, they come together in Rava's matter, and it applied to them; and if so, even on other limbs where there is no treifah — it depends; and even though eivar min hachai preceded in other limbs that stand for limbs — nevertheless treifah prohibition applied from miggo that it applies to limbs where treifah depends, like thigh, the like, etc. — it applies to all limbs of the animal inclusively; and it is an inclusive prohibition; if so, Rava who innovated this for us in limbs that became treifah in it — it is prohibition in a single body, and it applied from this; we learn the other of R' Yochanan that treifah applies to eivar min hachai in every death and in every manner it became treifah, from the reasoning of miggo, etc.; and one was stated from its associate — and examine, for it is correct and deep; and these are the words of the Rambam who summarized in one statement: he plucked a limb and rendered treifah — for it is prohibition in a single body; and he taught us this in that limb and the like the prohibition does not stand for limbs; and inclusive prohibition was innovated for us for all limbs; therefore he afterward wrote that he is liable for three, for treifah applied to the limb; and examine, for it is correct. And behold one should infer: why does treifah prohibition not apply to eivar min hachai — and we do not say from miggo that it applies to chelev in an animal, for chelev of treifah is forbidden, it should apply also to the animal itself, and it would be inclusive prohibition. And it is possible that therefore the Rambam holds chelev of treifah has no prohibition of negative commandment, only prohibition in general; and if so, miggo that it applies to chelev is not relevant, for it applied only to prohibition in general; and we require that prohibition of treifah negative commandment apply to eivar min hachai — and this does not exist. If one says in found treifah chelev found in the animal's innards — this is not nullified by the rule of treifah, only chelev that was formed afterward; and this is not because of the reason of treifah, only it is a species of animal and forbidden matter, and resembles broth and its sauce; but in eivar min hachai their broth and sauce are forbidden; but this is strained, for in eivar min hachai we do not forbid chelev since there is permission for eivar min hachai; and if so, there should still be miggo that it applies to chelev, for what is not relevant in eivar min hachai — since there is permission for its prohibition; and it is clear as Rosh wrote: in any case Taz wrote above in Laws of slaughter siman 24: that which we say in the Gemara chelev is permitted in eivar min hachai, for there is permission for its prohibition — and Taz explained: this means eivar min hachai prohibition is light in itself, since there is permission for its prohibition; it is not implied from this sugya; for if so, it would be appropriate for treifah prohibition to apply to eivar min hachai prohibition in a severe prohibition. However, this is difficult according to what Tosafot wrote in Yevamot chapter 2: one who comes upon his brother's wife and his wife's sister — they thought for R' Shimon he is liable because of his brother's wife, for it is not prohibition in a single body, for his sister's prohibition has permission for its prohibition when his wife dies, unlike his brother's wife where there is no permission, see there in Tosafot; and if so, that which the Gemara said why need the verse that eivar min hachai applies in impurity — let it be derived that its prohibition applies to a child of Noah; and the Gemara answers for R' Yehudah: so too it was needed only for R' Eliezer; and they further challenged: even for R' Eliezer according to the one who holds the prohibition stands for limbs — behold it is prohibition in a single body, see there; and it is difficult: perhaps R' Eliezer holds like R' Shimon, and eivar min hachai has permission for its prohibition in slaughter, unlike impurity; and if so, it is not prohibition in a single body, and impurity prohibition preceded; and requires further study.

rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.he: (בא"ד) ע"ש וזה ברור. עיין בספר תיבת גומא להגאון פורת יוסף זצ"ל פ' שמות אות א' בב"נ מסוכן אם שרי לישראל להושיט לו אמ"ה לרפאותו די"ל דוחי בהם ולא שימות בהם לישראל נאמר. אבל בב"נ לא הותר במקום פיקוח נפש ואיכא משום לפני עור:
rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.en: (In another place) See there, and this is clear. See in Sefer Teivat Guma of the Gaon Porat Yosef z"l, parashat Shemot ot 1: a child of Noah who is in danger — if it is permitted for Israel to give him eivar min hachai to heal him; one can say push aside in them and do not die in them was said regarding Israel; but for a child of Noah it was not permitted in a case of saving life, and there is lifnei iver.

kaf_hachayim.he: ב) שם. אבר מן החי אסור וכו' ולוקין עליו. ש"ך סק"א. פר"ח או' א' לה"פ או' א' ערוך השלחן או' א' והנ"מ אם לוקין עליו עיין לעיל סי' ט"ז סוף או' נ"ה יעו"ש. ועוד נ"מ לענין תיקון. ועיין לקמן או' ט'.
kaf_hachayim.en: (2) There. A limb from a living animal is forbidden, etc. — and one receives lashes for it. Shach s.k. 1. Peri Chadash ot 1; Lechem HaPanim ot 1; Arukh HaShulchan ot 1; and the practical difference whether one receives lashes for it — see above siman 16 end of ot 55, see there; and another practical difference regarding repair; and see below ot 9.

kereti.he:
אסור וכ' הטור דאין נוהג בטמאה ועיין פלתי מ"ש בישוב קושייתם דמה נ"מ סוף כל סוף אסור ומה לי משום אמ"ה או משום טמאה ע"ש ואם חל על טריפה עיין פלתי מ"ש בישוב דברי רמב"ם מה שהפר"ח עמד בו וכן הלח"מ ישב בדוחק ועמ"ש ועכ"פ לדינא חל אף בטריפה. והנ"מ הוא כמ"ש בטמאה:
ובשר הפורש וכו' ולפי דקיי"ל אסורים מבטלים זא"ז א"כ אם נתערב כזית בשר כשר וכזית בשר מהחי וכזית אבר מהחי הרי זה בטל דאסורים מבטלין וכן להיפוך כזית טריפה וכזית בשר כשר וכזית בשר מהחי אין בטל דתרווייהו טריפה נינהו ואינה מבטלים ולכך דייק הש"ע אסור משום בשר בשדה טריפה:
kereti.en:
Forbidden. And the Tur wrote that it does not apply in an impure animal; and see Peleti what I wrote in resolving their difficulty: what practical difference, in the end it is forbidden; and what difference to me whether because of eivar min hachai or because of impurity, see there; and if it applies to treifah — see Peleti what I wrote in resolving the words of the Rambam, that which Peri Chadash stood on, and so Lechem Mishneh strained himself; and in any case for practical law it applies also to treifah; and the practical difference is as written regarding impurity.
And flesh that separated, etc. And according to what we hold — forbidden items nullify one another — if so, if an olive-bulk of kosher flesh mixed with an olive-bulk of flesh from a living animal and an olive-bulk of limb from a living animal, behold it is nullified, for forbidden items nullify; and likewise the reverse: an olive-bulk of treifah and an olive-bulk of kosher flesh and an olive-bulk of flesh from a living animal — it is not nullified, for both are treifah and do not nullify; therefore the Shulchan Aruch was precise: forbidden because of flesh in the field treifah.

mechaber.he: אבר או בשר המדולדלים אם אינו יכול לחזור ולחיות אפי' אם לא פירש ממנו עד לאחר שחיטה אסור: הגה ועיין לעיל סימן נ"ה יתרת העומדת במקום שאינה מטריף הבהמה מותר לאכלה ולא אמרינן יתר כנטול דמי והוי כאבר המדולדל (א"ו הארוך) אבר הנשמט ממקומו במקום שאינו מטריף הבהמה מותר לאכלו אף אם אין עור ובשר חופין רובו (רשב"א סי' ס"ט) אבל המנהג להחמיר גם בזה (א"ו הארוך):
mechaber.en: A limb or flesh that is dangling — if it cannot return and live, even if it did not separate from the animal until after slaughter — it is forbidden. {Rama: And see above siman 55: the cauda equina standing in a place that does not render the animal treifah is permitted to eat, and we do not say the extra portion is considered as removed and is like a dangling limb (Or Zarua, HaArukh). A limb that slipped from its place in a place that does not render the animal treifah is permitted to eat it even if skin and flesh do not cover most of it (Rashba siman 69). But the custom is to be stringent also in this (Or Zarua, HaArukh).}

siftei_kohen.he:
אם אינו יכול כו'. אבל כשיכול לחזור ולחיות אם נשחטה הבהמה מותר עכ"ל טור ורמב"ם ור"ל אבל אם מתה אינו חייב עליו משום אבר מן החי אלא משום נבלה וכ"כ הרב המגיד שם ופשוט:
אינו יכול כו'. וסיים הטור ועצם הנשבר אם עור ובשר חופים את רובו מותר כו' וכ"כ הרמב"ם שם ומשמע מדבריהם דברישא דהיינו במדולדל אין חילוק בין עור ובשר חופים את רובו אלא בין אם יכול לחזור ולחיות או לא והיינו דוקא במדולדל ממש דהיינו שנעקר ממקומו לגמרי ומחובר קצת אבל כשנשמט ממקומו האבר ועדיין מעורה בגידיו היינו הך דכתב הר"ב בהג"ה ויתבאר בסמוך (וע"ל סי' נ"ה ס"ק ז'):
שחיטה. וכתב הרמב"ם שם ואם מתה הבהמה רואין אותה כאלו נפל מחיים לפיכך לוקין עליו משום אבר מן החי עכ"ל וכ' הרב המגיד שם שהוציא דין זה מהש"ס:
אסור. ופירש הרב המגיד שם משום אבר מן החי משום מצות פרישה מדרבנן:
וע"ל סי' נ"ה. סעיף ה' אם נמלח עם שאר בשר ושאר דיניו נתבארו שם על נכון:
יתרת כו'. ע"ל סי' מ"ג ס"ק ט' וסימן נ"ד ס"ק ט':
במקום שאינו מטריף. ובמקום שמטריף ע"ל סימן נ"ה ס"ק ז':
מותר לאכלו כו'. דדמי לביצים שנתלשו דשריין דכיון דלא מסרחן אית ביה חיותא ואבר זה שנשמט ועדיין מעורה בגידיו ודאי לא מסרח וכל דלא מסרח חיותא אית ביה ושרי עכ"ל תשו' רשב"א שם ולפ"ז משמע אפילו אינו יכול לחזור ולחיות שרי כדמשמע בש"ס גבי ביצים שנתלשו ואע"ג דבאבר המדולדל נתבאר כל שאינו יכול לחזור ולחיות אסור היינו משום שאינה מעורה כלל בגידין ומ"מ קשה דהרשב"א אזיל לטעמיה דמתיר בביצים שנתלשו וכמ"ש הרב המגיד וב"י בשמו אבל למאי דק"ל כהרמב"ם דביצים שנתלשו נהגו ישראל לאסור א"כ ה"ה בנשמט אבר וכן כתב הרמב"ם בהדיא פ"ה מהמ"א דין ז' וז"ל שמט אבר או מעכו או דכו כגון הביצים שמעכן או כתתן ה"ז אינו אסור מן התורה שהרי יש בו מקצת חיות ולפיכך אינו מסריח ואעפ"כ אסור לאכלו ממנהג שנהגו כל ישראל מקודם שהרי הוא דומה לאבר מן החי עכ"ל וכן מ"ש הרב בהג"ה שהמנהג להחמיר גם בזה הוא ע"פ מ"ש בד"מ כן בשם או"ה כלל נ' דין י"א ובאו"ה שם לא הביא אלא דברי הרמב"ם הנ"ל ונראה דאה"נ קאמר הר"ב מותר לאכלו מדינא כמו בביצים אבל המנהג להחמיר גם בזה כמו בבצים:
אבל המנהג להחמיר גם בזה. משמע אפי' עור ובשר חופים את רובו וכן משמע ברמב"ם שם שאח"ז כתב נשבר העצם אם עור ובשר חופים את רובו כו' משמע דברישא בנשמט אין חילוק בין עור ובשר חופים את רובו או לא אבל הכל בו בהל' איסור והיתר גבי בוקא דאטמא דשף מדוכתי' קודם ד"ה בהמה שנקרעת בה רוב הבשר החופה את הכרס כו' מחלק גבי נשמט הגף ג"כ בין עור ובשר חופים את רובו או לא ע"ש מיהו כל זה בנשמט אבל בנשבר ע"ל סי' נ"ה סעיף ה' נתבארו דיניו כי שם מקומן. והעט"ז השמיט כל דינים אלו דנשמט שכתב הר"ב והכניס דינים אחרים דנשבר תחתיהם ולאו שפיר עביד:
siftei_kohen.en:
If it cannot, etc. But when it can return and live — if the animal was slaughtered, it is permitted, end of his words — Tur and Rambam; and Rashi explained: but if it died, he is not liable for it because of eivar min hachai, but because of nevelah; and so wrote Rav HaMagid there; and it is simple:
It cannot, etc. And the Tur concluded: and a broken bone — if skin and flesh cover most of it, it is permitted, etc.; and so wrote the Rambam there; and it is implied from their words that at the outset — meaning in a dangling limb — there is no distinction whether skin and flesh cover most of it, but only whether it can return and live or not; and this is specifically in a truly dangling limb — meaning it was uprooted from its place entirely and is connected a bit; but when the limb slipped from its place and is still wrapped in its sinews — this is that which Rav Beit Yosef wrote in the hagahah, and it will be explained shortly (and see above siman 55 s.k. 7):
Slaughter. And the Rambam wrote there: and if the animal died, we view it as if it fell from life; therefore one receives lashes for it because of eivar min hachai, end of his words; and Rav HaMagid wrote there that he derived this law from the Talmud:
Forbidden. And Rav HaMagid explained there — because of eivar min hachai, because of the mitzvah of separation rabbinically:
And see above siman 55. Seif 5 — if it was salted with other flesh, and the rest of its laws were explained there, on the correct understanding:
The extra portion, etc. See above siman 43 s.k. 9 and siman 54 s.k. 9:
In a place that does not render treifah. And in a place that does render treifah — see above siman 55 s.k. 7:
Permitted to eat it, etc. For it is similar to eggs that were plucked — they are permitted, for since they do not rot, there is life-force in them; and this limb that slipped and is still wrapped in its sinews certainly does not rot; and anything that does not rot has life-force in it and is permitted, end of his words — Rashba there; and accordingly it is implied that even if it cannot return and live it is permitted, as is implied in the Talmud regarding eggs that were plucked; and even though in a dangling limb it was explained that whatever cannot return and live is forbidden — that deals with what is not wrapped at all in sinews; nevertheless it is difficult, for Rashba follows his reasoning that he permits eggs that were plucked, as Rav HaMagid and Beit Yosef wrote in his name; but according to what appears correct to us, like the Rambam — eggs that were plucked, Israel practiced to forbid — if so, the same applies to a slipped limb; and so the Rambam wrote explicitly chapter 5 of Forbidden Foods din 7 — and these are his words: a limb slipped, or was crushed, or was flattened, such as eggs that were crushed or ground — this is not forbidden from the Torah, for there is in it a measure of life-force; therefore it does not rot; nevertheless it is forbidden to eat from the custom that all Israel practiced from before, for it resembles eivar min hachai, end of his words; and so wrote Rav Beit Yosef in the hagahah that the custom to be stringent also in this is according to what Darkei Moshe wrote thus in the name of Or Zarua general rule 50 din 11; and in Or Zarua there he brought only the words of the Rambam mentioned above; and it appears that therefore Rav Beit Yosef says it is permitted to eat from the law, like eggs; but the custom is to be stringent also in this, like eggs:
But the custom is to be stringent also in this. It is implied even if skin and flesh cover most of it; and so is implied in the Rambam there, who afterward wrote: the bone broke — if skin and flesh cover most of it, etc.; it is implied that at the outset, in a slipped limb, there is no distinction whether skin and flesh cover most of it or not; but it is all in the laws of prohibition and permission regarding the case of the impure animal that was slaughtered from its place, before s.v. beheimah shenikra'at bah rov habasar hachof et hakereis etc., he distinguishes also regarding a slipped body whether skin and flesh cover most of it or not, see there; however, all this is in a slipped limb; but in a broken bone — see above siman 55 seif 5 — its laws were explained, for there is its place. And Taz omitted all these laws of slipped limb that Rav Beit Yosef wrote, and inserted other laws of broken bone in their place — and he did not act properly:

turei_zahav.he: אבר הנשמט. פי' ולא נשבר כתוב בד"מ וז"ל כתוב באו"ה אבר המדולדל אסור אפי' חזר ונקשר היטב מאחר שנאסר פעם אחת אין לו היתר עוד חיישינן שמא לא הבריא יפה כל צרכו עכ"ל ולא נראה דאם אנו אומרים הואיל ונקשר דודאי לא יצא לחוץ לענין היתר הבהמה כמ"ש הטור סי' נ"ה אע"פ שהוא חשש טרפה דאורייתא כ"ש שאנו סומכין על זו לענין איסור אבר המדולדל שהוא דרבנן עכ"ל:
turei_zahav.en: The slipped limb. Meaning: and not broken — it is written in Darkei Moshe — and these are his words: it is written in Or Zarua: a dangling limb is forbidden even if it returned and was bound well, since once it was forbidden once it has no permission again; we are concerned perhaps it did not heal well enough, end of his words; and it does not appear that if we say since it was bound, certainly it did not go outside — for the matter of permitting the animal, as the Tur wrote siman 55 — even though it is a concern of treifah d'oraisa, all the more so we rely on this for the prohibition of a dangling limb, which is rabbinical, end of his words.

baer_heitev.he:
אסור. פי' הרב המגיד משום מצות פרישה מדרבנן וכ' הש"ך דאם יכול לחזור ולחיות אם נשחטה הבהמה מותר אבל אם מתה אינו חייב עליו משום אמ"ה אלא משום נבילה ואם אינו יכול לחזור ולחיות ומתה הבהמה פסק הרמב"ם דרואין אותה כאלו נפל מחיים ולוקין עליו משום אמ"ה ובאבר המדולדל אין חילוק בין עור ובשר חופין את רובו או לא רק החילוק הוא אם יכול לחזור ולחיות ודוקא אם נעקר ממקומו לגמרי ומחובר קצת אבל כשנשמט ממקומו ועדיין מעורה בגידיו היינו הך דכתב הר"ב בהג"ה:
לעיל. שם ס"ה נתבאר אם נמלח עם שאר בשר מה דינו ע"ש:
הנשמט. כתב בד"מ בשם או"ה אבר המדולדל אפילו חזר ונקשר היטב אסור ול"נ דאם סומכים לענין היתר הבהמה לומר דודאי לא יצא לחוץ אע"פ שהוא חשש טריפות דאורייתא כ"ש שיש לסמוך ע"ז באיסור דרבנן עכ"ל:
לאכלו. דדמי לביצים שנתלשו (דכיון דלא מסרחן אית בהו חיותא אף אף על גב דבאבר המדולדל נתבאר דאם אינו יכול לחזור ולחיות אסור התם איירי שאינו מעורה כלל אבל הכא עדיין מעורה בגידין). אבל המנהג להחמיר אפי' עור ובשר חופין את רובו. ש"ך:
baer_heitev.en:
Forbidden. Rav HaMagid explained — because of the mitzvah of separation rabbinically; and Shach wrote that if it can return and live — if the animal was slaughtered, it is permitted; but if it died, he is not liable for it because of eivar min hachai but because of nevelah; and if it cannot return and live and the animal died — the Rambam ruled that we view it as if it fell from life and one receives lashes for it because of eivar min hachai. And in a dangling limb there is no distinction whether skin and flesh cover most of it or not; the distinction is only whether it can return and live — and specifically if it was uprooted from its place entirely and is connected a bit; but when it slipped from its place and is still wrapped in its sinews — this is that which Rav Beit Yosef wrote in the hagahah.
Above. There siman 55 it was explained — if it was salted with other flesh, what is its law, see there.
The slipped one. Darkei Moshe wrote in the name of Or Zarua: a dangling limb — even if it returned and was bound well — is forbidden; and in my humble opinion, if we rely for permitting the animal to say that certainly it did not go outside — even though it is a concern of treifot d'oraisa, all the more so one should rely on this in a rabbinical prohibition, end of his words.
To eat it. For it is similar to eggs that were plucked (for since they do not rot, there is life-force in them; even though in a dangling limb it was explained that if it cannot return and live it is forbidden — there it deals with what is not wrapped at all; but here it is still wrapped in sinews). But the custom is to be stringent even if skin and flesh cover most of it. Shach.

beer_hagolah.he:
ברייתא דף ע"ג:
רמב"ם פ"ה מהלכות מאכלות אסורות ונלמד מדין ביצי הזכר:
beer_hagolah.en:
Baraita daf 73:
Rambam chapter 5 of Laws of Forbidden Foods; and we learn from the law of male eggs:

beur_hagra.he: אבר הנשמט כו'. ז"ל הרשב"א לא שמענו עור ובשר אלא בנשבר העצם הא בשמוטה לא ולכך לא חילקו בבוקא דאטמא בין עור ובשר כו' ותדע שהרי ביעי חשילתא הוי כאבר הנשמט ושריין משום דאית בהו חיותא כמ"ש בס"ד וה"ה לאבר שנשמט ועדיין מעורה בגידיו ולא מסרח וכל דלא מסרח חיותא אית בהו כמ"ש בביעי וז"ל הרמב"ם בפ"ה שמט אבר כו' כגון הביצים כו' וכ"ה בתוספתא הנ"ל אבר מדולדל כו' נשבר העצם כו' מכלל דאבר המדולדל הוא שנשמט ואמר דתליא ביש להעלות ארוכה ולא בעור ובשר וז"ש בגמ' גבי ביעי חיותא אית בהו ואף שאמרו שם ואת לא כו' משום דלא בריין כמ"ש שם משא"כ כאן דמיירי בשיכול להיות כנ"ל:
beur_hagra.en: The slipped limb, etc. Thus Rashba: we did not hear skin and flesh except in a broken bone; here in a slipped one — no; therefore they did not distinguish in the case of the impure animal slaughtered from its place between skin and flesh etc.; and know that soft eggs are like a slipped limb and are permitted because there is life-force in them, as written in siman 64; and the same for a limb that slipped and is still wrapped in its sinews and does not rot — anything that does not rot has life-force in it, as written regarding eggs; and thus the Rambam chapter 5: a limb slipped etc., such as eggs etc.; and so in the Tosefta mentioned above: dangling limb etc., the bone broke etc.; from which is implied that a dangling limb is one that slipped; and he said it depends on whether there is in it to raise a long piece, and not on skin and flesh; and this is what the Gemara says regarding eggs: there is life-force in them; and even though they said there and you not etc. — because they do not heal, as written there; unlike here, which deals with what can be, as explained.

pitchei_teshuva.he: אבר הפורש. עי' בה"ט ועי' בש"ך דטעם השגתו על הב"ח הוא דהא קי"ל דלנכרים נוהג גם בטמאה וא"כ אסור להושיט להם ועי' בתשובת אמונת שמואל סימן י"ד שכתב ליישב דבריהם ועשה כלל חדש דהיכא דשרי לדידיה ואינו אוסר אלא לב"נ שרי לאושוטי דלא דמי למושיט כוס יין לנזיר אף דלדידיה שרי מ"מ התורה אסרה עליו כשיהיה נזיר אבל באיסור דשרי לדידיה כמו אמ"ה בטמאים שרי להושיט לב"נ ואינו מוזהר על לפ"ע והא דנקיט בפרישה לישנא דמי איכא מידי אאיסור הושטה קאי עכ"ד ע"ש. ולכאורה יש ראייה לדבריו מפסחים דף כ"ב והרי אמ"ה כו' הא לכלבים שרי ע"ש ועיין בתוס' שם ובש"ך לעיל סימן כ"ז ודו"ק ומ"מ לדינא צ"ע:
pitchei_teshuva.en: The separated limb. See Bach; and see in Shach that the reason for his challenge on Bach is that we hold that for idolaters it applies also in impurity; and if so, it is forbidden to give it to them; and see in responsa Emunat Shmuel siman 14 that he wrote to reconcile their words; and he made a new principle: where it is permitted for him and he forbids only for a child of Noah — it is permitted to give, for it is not similar to giving a cup of wine to a nazir, for even though for him it is permitted, nevertheless the Torah forbade him when he becomes a nazir; but in a prohibition that is permitted for him, like eivar min hachai in impure animals — it is permitted to give to a child of Noah, and he is not warned regarding lifnei iver; and that which he cited in separation the language who is there anything — it refers to the prohibition of giving, thus end of his words, see there. And at first glance there is proof for his words from Pesachim daf 22: and behold eivar min hachai etc. — behold for dogs it is permitted, see there; and see in Tosafot there and in Shach above siman 27; and requires further study; and nevertheless for practical law requires further study.

peleti.he: אבר או בשר וכו' בגמ' אמרינן שאין בו אלא מצות פרוש ולדעת הרמב"ם היינו דאין בו מלקות אבל איסורא דאורייתא איכא ונתן המ"מ הטעם מידי דהוי חצי שיעור דאתרבי מן כל ומ"מ לא אתרבי רק לאיסור ולא למלקות ופר"ח דחה דכיון דליכא שיעורא לא שייך ביה אכיל' ולכך לית בי' מלקות ודברי המ"מ נכונים דתינח חצי שיעור הא כוי למ"ד ברי' בפ"ע היא אתרבי ג"כ ביומא מן כל ואית ביה רק אסורא ולא מלקות ומה יאמר בזה הפ"ח והמ"מ חדא מנייהו נקט אלא ש"מ דאיתרב' לאיסורא ולא למלקות וה"ה באבר מדולדל ודעת התוס' ורש"י ויתר מפרשים דעתם מצות פרוש אסור דרבנן לפרוש מאיסור דאורייתא עי"כ אבל איסור תורה לית בהן והפר"ח הביא לדברי הרמב"ם ראיה מן תוס' דע"ז דקתני בהו דאבר ובשר מדולדלין אסורין לישראל ולבן נח ואלו מצוה דרבנן בן נח מה טיבו לאסור אבל יש להבין הך מצות פרוש ילפינן בגמ' מן ריבוי דבשר בשדה טריפה לא תאכלו ומה ענין ב"נ להך קרא בשר בשדה טריפה ועיין מש"ל דעמדנו בשם הכ"מ ורשב"א על בשר הפורש מהחי דנולד מן בשר בשדה טריפה דמה ענין ב"נ גבי' וכל מש"ל בישובו אין עולים כאן ולכן נראה לפי' רש"י דרבנן אסרו לאבר ובשר מדולדל וסמכו אקרא י"ל כי אסורו שווינהו כאמ"ה לגמרי דאף לב"נ יאסור כדי שלא יהי' הבדל בו לבין אמ"ה גמור. וסברה זו כתבי מקצת מחברים עי' לעיל סי' נ"ה ולרמב"ם צ"ל דמיירי דחתך לאברים מדולדלין בבהמה מקדם והוא חתכן לאחר שחיטה ואתרבי מקרא לאוסרן. ולב"נ לית להו שחיטה אסור ג"כ דמי יתירן. ואפי' למאן דמתיר מפרכסת משום מי איכא מידי אבל בזה הא גם בישראל אסור ודוק כי נכון הארכתי בזה קצת הואיל וש"ע קיצר והדינים גופי תורה אמרתי טוב להאריך קצת ולהעיר אוזן לומדים:
peleti.en: Limb or flesh, etc. — in the Gemara we say that there is in it only the mitzvah of separation; and according to the Rambam, this means there are no lashes, but there is d'oraisa prohibition; and Mishneh Lamelech gave the reason like half a measure that was included from kol, and nevertheless it was included only for prohibition and not for lashes; and Peri Chadash rejected: since there is no measure, eating is not relevant, therefore there are no lashes; and Mishneh Lamelech's words are correct: let it be resolved half a measure — behold according to the one who says it is a creature by itself, it was also included in Yoma from kol, and there is in it only prohibition and not lashes — what will Peri Chadash and Mishneh Lamelech say on this; one of them took it; only we learn that it was included for prohibition and not for lashes; and the same applies to dangling limb. And the view of Tosafot and Rashi and most commentators: their view is mitzvah of separation — forbidden rabbinically to separate from d'oraisa prohibition; therefore; but d'oraisa prohibition does not exist in them; and Peri Chadash brought for the Rambam's words proof from Tosafot Avodah Zarah that teaches dangling limb and flesh are forbidden for Israel and for a child of Noah — and if it is a rabbinical commandment, what is its nature to forbid a child of Noah; but one must understand this mitzvah of separation — we derive in the Gemara from the extension of flesh in the field treifah you shall not eat; and what relevance does a child of Noah have to this verse flesh in the field treifah; and see what I wrote that we stood in the name of Kesef Mishneh and Rashba on flesh that separated from a living animal that is born from flesh in the field treifah — what relevance does a child of Noah have to it; and all that I wrote in its reconciliation does not apply here; therefore it appears according to Rashi's explanation that the rabbis forbade limb and dangling flesh, and they relied on a verse — one can say that its prohibition they equated to full eivar min hachai, that also for a child of Noah it should be forbidden so there would not be a difference between it and full eivar min hachai. And this reasoning several authors wrote; see above siman 55; and for the Rambam it must deal with that he cut into dangling limbs in the animal beforehand, and he cut them after slaughter, and the verse was extended to forbid them; and for a child of Noah they have no slaughter — forbidden also, for who will permit them; and even for the one who permits still convulsing because of who is there anything — but in this even for Israel it is forbidden; and examine, for it is correct; I elaborated a bit here since the Shulchan Aruch abbreviated, and the laws themselves of Torah — I said it is good to elaborate a bit and to awaken the ear of learners.

kaf_hachayim.he: ג) שם. אסור בבהמה חיה ועוף. אבל לא בדגים וחגבים. ש"ך סק"ב. כנה"ג בהגה"ט או' י"ב. פר"ח או' ב' לה"פ או' ב' שפ"ד או' ב' חכ"א כלל כ"ז או' א' ביא"ב בשפ"ז או' ב' זב"צ או' א' ועיין לעיל סי' י"ג סעי' א' בהגה ובדברינו לשם בס"ד.
kaf_hachayim.en: (3) There. Forbidden in domesticated animal, undomesticated animal, and fowl; but not in fish and locusts. Shach s.k. 2. Knesset HaGedolah in Hagahot Taz ot 12; Peri Chadash ot 2; Lechem HaPanim ot 2; Shaarei De'ah ot 2; Chochmat Adam general rule 27 ot 1; Beit Yosef BeShulchan Aruch HaZahav ot 2; Zivchei Tzedek ot 1; and see above siman 13 seif 1 in the hagahah and our words there, with Heaven's help.

kereti.he:
אבר ובשר מדולדלין עיין פלתי שיש בזה מחלוקת הרמב"ם ומחברים דלדעת הרמב"ם מהתורה אסור וליתר מחברים מדרבנן. ולב"נ עיין פלתי שכתבתי לדעת דסוברין מדרבנן י"ל דגם בזו שווינהו רבנן כאמ"ה גמור לאסור בב"נ אבל לרמב"ם אם חתכם לאברים מדולדלים אחר שחיטה יש לאסור לב"נ אבל אם חתכן אחר שמתה מותר לב"נ וצ"ע:
אבר הנשמט באבר ובשר המדולדלין תלוי הכל אם יכול לחזור ולחיות אבל גבי נשמט תלוי הכל בעור ובשר חופין את רובו כ"כ אחרונים ובאמת היא דאם אין חופין רובו אינו יכול לחזור ולחיות וע"ל סימן נ"ז:
kereti.en:
Limb and dangling flesh — see Peleti that there is a dispute between the Rambam and authors: according to the Rambam from the Torah it is forbidden; according to other authors rabbinically. And in my humble opinion see Peleti that I wrote: according to those who hold rabbinically, one can say that also in this the rabbis equated it to full eivar min hachai to forbid for a child of Noah; but according to the Rambam, if one cut them into dangling limbs after slaughter, one must forbid for a child of Noah; but if one cut them after it died, it is permitted for a child of Noah; and requires further study.
The slipped limb — in limb and dangling flesh everything depends on whether it can return and live; but regarding slipped, everything depends on whether skin and flesh cover most of it, so wrote the later authorities; and in truth, if they do not cover most of it, it cannot return and live; and see above siman 57.

mechaber.he: ביצי זכר שנתלשו ועדיין הם מעורים בכיסם אינו אסור מן התורה שהרי יש בו מקצת חיות ולפיכך אינו מסריח ואעפ"כ אסור לאכלו ממנהג שנהגו ישראל שלא לאכלו מפני שדומה לאבר מן החי:
mechaber.en: Male eggs that were plucked and are still wrapped in their sac are not forbidden from the Torah, for there is in them a measure of life-force; therefore they do not rot; nevertheless it is forbidden to eat them — from the custom that Israel practiced not to eat them because they resemble a limb from a living animal.

beer_hagolah.he: פלוגתא דרב אמי ורב אסי דף צ"ג וכר' יוחנן שם.
beer_hagolah.en: Dispute of Rav Ami and Rav Assi daf 93, and like R' Yochanan there.

beur_hagra.he: ממנהג כו'. רמב"ם. דאנן בתר בני בבל גרירן. ר"ן:
beur_hagra.en: From the custom, etc. Rambam. For we follow the children of Babylon. Ran.

kaf_hachayim.he: ד) שם. אסור בבהמה חיה ועוף. הטהורים אבל לא בטמאים. הרמב"ם ריש פ"ה מה' מ"א. טור. ב"י. ב"ח. ט"ז סק"א. ש"ך סק"ג פר"ח או' ג' שו"ג או' א' ומ"מ אסור להושיט לבני נח אבר מ"ה אף מן הטמאים משום דלדידהו בהמה טמאה ג"כ שריא ואסור לאכול ממנה אמ"ה ואסור להושיט להם משום ולפני עור וכו' ש"ך שם בשם הש"ס וכמה פו' דלא כהב"ח יעו"ש. וכ"כ הפר"ח שם לאסור ולדחות דברי המתירים יעו"ש וכ"כ המחב"ר או' א' לדחות ולהחזיק דברי הפר"ח יעוש"ב. וכ"פ ערוך השלחן או' ד' חכ"א שם. ביא"ב בשפ"ז שם.
kaf_hachayim.en: (4) There. Forbidden in domesticated animal, undomesticated animal, and fowl — the pure, but not the impure. Rambam beginning of chapter 5 of Forbidden Foods; Tur; Beit Yosef; Bach; Taz s.k. 1; Shach s.k. 3; Peri Chadash ot 3; Shulchan Gavoah ot 1; and nevertheless it is forbidden to give children of Noah eivar min hachai even from impure animals, because for them impure animal is also permitted, and it is forbidden to eat from it eivar min hachai; and it is forbidden to give them because of lifnei iver etc. — Shach there in the name of the Talmud; and several poskim not like Bach, see there; and so Peri Chadash there to forbid and to reject the words of those who permit, see there; and so Machberet ot 1 to reject and to uphold the words of Peri Chadash, see there; and so Arukh HaShulchan ot 4; Chochmat Adam there; Beit Yosef BeShulchan Aruch HaZahav there.
